items.title: Create server/services/securityPipeline.js
items.details: Create c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\PrismGuard-SecureAI-main\server\services\securityPipeline.js. Export analyzePrompt(content, resourceId) async function. Stage 1 - Keyword Filter: query db for enabled security_rules, check each pattern case-insensitively against content, if match return blocked result with that rule's severity. Stage 2 - Secure AI API: POST to process.env.SECURE_GUARD_API_URL+'/analyze' with Authorization: Bearer SECURE_GUARD_TOKEN header, body {prompt: content, context: 'security_analysis'}, timeout 8s using node-fetch. If fetch fails/timeout: use demo engine (check for: ignore, bypass, jailbreak, override, reveal, export all, grant me access, admin mode, developer mode, system prompt, you are now, pretend you are, act as - if 2+ match: blocked with prompt_injection; if 1 match: review with medium risk; else: pass). Stage 3 - Resource Detection: if resourceId provided use it; else keyword-match content (banking/interest/account/financial/transaction/balance -> 'banking', government/policy/regulation/scheme/official/ministry -> 'government', company/employee/salary/revenue/hr/internal/department -> 'company', research/paper/quantum/dataset/study/academic -> 'research', default 'banking'). Stage 4 - ML Inference: POST to process.env.ML_SERVICE_URL+'/predict' with {prompt: content, resource: detectedResource}, timeout 8s. If ML unavailable: use keyword demo result (demoMode=true). Use ML result if available: apply thresholds (risk_score > 0.65 = blocked, > 0.40 = review, else allowed). If allowed: generate response by POST to LLM_BASE_URL+'/chat/completions' with Authorization: Bearer LLM_API_KEY, model: LLM_MODEL, messages: [{role:'system', content:'You are PrismGuard secure AI for '+resource+' queries. Answer helpfully.'},{role:'user',content:content}]. If LLM fails: use mock responses per resource. Return {status, riskLevel, riskScore, attackType, blockedLayer, reason, resource, pipeline:[{stage,status,detail}], response, mlUsed, demoMode}.

items.title: Create ml-service/app/model_registry.py
items.details: Create c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\PrismGuard-SecureAI-main\ml-service\app\model_registry.py. Class ModelRegistry: __init__ creates self._models = {} dict and self._metadata = {}. load_model(resource: str): find latest DEPLOYED version in models/{resource}/ by scanning subdirs sorted descending, load model.joblib + vectorizer.joblib + attack_classifier.joblib + metadata.json using joblib.load(), store in self._models[resource] = {model, vectorizer, attack_classifier, metadata}. get_model(resource): return self._models.get(resource, None). reload_model(resource, version=None): re-run load_model(resource). list_models(): return {r: {version, accuracy, status, training_samples} for r in _models}. load_all_resources(): call load_model for each resource in RESOURCES, log warnings for missing models (do not crash). is_loaded(resource): bool.

items.title: Create ml-service/app/training.py
items.details: Create c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\PrismGuard-SecureAI-main\ml-service\app\training.py. Import pandas, numpy, sklearn (TfidfVectorizer, LogisticRegression, train_test_split, classification_report, accuracy_score, precision_recall_fscore_support), joblib, json, Path, datetime. Function train_resource_model(resource: str, extra_samples: list = []) -> dict: 1) Load base CSV from DATASETS_DIR/resource/{resource}_prompts.csv as pandas DataFrame. 2) If extra_samples: append as rows to DataFrame. 3) Validate: len >= 10, both 'safe' and 'malicious' labels present, else raise ValueError. 4) X = df['prompt'], y_binary = (df['label']=='malicious').astype(int), y_attack = df['attack_type']. 5) Train/test split 80/20 stratified on y_binary. 6) Binary pipeline: TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), max_features=5000, sublinear_tf=True) + LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=1000, class_weight='balanced'). Fit on train. 7) Attack type classifier: filter malicious samples only, if >= 5 malicious samples: TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), max_features=3000) + LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=500, multi_class='multinomial'), fit on malicious subset. 8) Evaluate binary classifier: accuracy, precision, recall, f1 (weighted), confusion_matrix.tolist(). 9) Determine next version: scan MODELS_DIR/resource/ for existing vN dirs, increment. 10) Save to MODELS_DIR/resource/v{N}/: model.joblib (full sklearn Pipeline), vectorizer.joblib (the fitted TfidfVectorizer), attack_classifier.joblib (or None if < 5 malicious), metadata.json = {version: 'v{N}', resource, trained_at: ISO string, training_samples: len(df), accuracy, precision, recall, f1, confusion_matrix, model_type: 'tfidf_lr', status: 'DEPLOYED'}. 11) Return metrics dict.

items.title: Create ml-service/app/inference.py
items.details: Create c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\PrismGuard-SecureAI-main\ml-service\app\inference.py. Import config, schemas. Function predict(prompt: str, resource: str, registry) -> PredictResponse: 1) model_data = registry.get_model(resource). 2) If None: return demo_mode=True result using keyword heuristics (check for: ignore, bypass, jailbreak, override, reveal, export, grant.*access, admin mode, developer mode, system prompt, act as, pretend, you are now). If 2+ keywords match: status=blocked, risk_score=0.85, attack_type=prompt_injection. If 1 keyword: status=review, risk_score=0.55. Else: status=allowed, risk_score=0.1. 3) If model loaded: vectorizer = model_data['vectorizer'], model = model_data['model']. features = vectorizer.transform([prompt]). proba = model.predict_proba(features)[0]. malicious_prob = proba[1]. Apply thresholds from config. 4) Attack type: if attack_classifier loaded and status!=allowed: use attack_classifier to predict attack_type. 5) matched_signals: get feature names from vectorizer, find top 5 features with highest weight in the transformed vector that are present in prompt. 6) reason: build human-readable string based on attack_type and matched_signals. 7) Return PredictResponse with all fields populated.

items.title: Create ml-service/app/main.py
items.details: Create c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\PrismGuard-SecureAI-main\ml-service\app\main.py. FastAPI app with lifespan: on startup create ModelRegistry(), call registry.load_all_resources(), store as app.state.registry. Endpoints: GET /health -> {status:'ok', models_loaded:{resource:version}}. GET /models -> list all models from registry.list_models(). GET /models/{resource} -> single model info or 404. POST /predict -> call inference.predict(req.prompt, req.resource, app.state.registry), return PredictResponse. POST /train -> body: TrainRequest, generate job_id=uuid, store job in in-memory dict jobs[job_id]={status:'queued',progress:0}, run training in asyncio background task (call training.train_resource_model(resource, samples), update job progress at each stage: preparing=20, training=60, evaluating=80, completed=100, reload registry after completion), return TrainResponse immediately. POST /retrain -> same as /train. GET /training/status/{job_id} -> return TrainingStatusResponse from jobs dict. POST /add-sample -> append {prompt,label,attack_type} row to datasets/{resource}/{resource}_prompts.csv, return {success:True}. Handle errors: model not found -> 404, training failure -> update job status to 'failed' with error_message.
